units.title: Humanists
units.blurb: Erasmus, Machiavelli, Rabelais and Montaigne: new looks at people, power and the self.

units.title: A New Sky
units.blurb: Copernicus puts the sun at the center.

units.title: Shakespeare
units.blurb: The comedies, histories, tragedies, romances and sonnets.

units.title: Cervantes
units.blurb: Don Quixote, the knight who read too many books.

topics.title: Erasmus: The Praise of Folly
topics.short: Folly herself gives a speech in her own honor, mocking the vanity of scholars, rulers and churchmen.

topics.title: Machiavelli: The Prince
topics.short: Advice to a new ruler on how power is won and kept, looking at how people act rather than how they should.

topics.title: Rabelais: Gargantua and Pantagruel
topics.short: Giant comedy about two giants, full of learning and nonsense, with an abbey whose only rule is 'Do what you will.'

topics.title: Montaigne: Essays
topics.short: The man who invented the essay tries out his thoughts on everything, above all on himself.

topics.title: Calvin: Institutes of the Christian Religion
topics.short: A Reformation leader's ordered account of Christian teaching, from knowing God and ourselves to the church.

topics.title: Copernicus: On the Revolutions
topics.short: The sun, not the Earth, at the center: the book that set the planets in a new order.

topics.title: Shakespeare: The Comedies
topics.short: Lovers lost in woods and disguises, fools wiser than lords, and everything set right by the last act.

topics.title: Shakespeare: Romeo and Juliet
topics.short: Two young people from feuding families, and how haste and hatred bring about their deaths.

topics.title: Shakespeare: The History Plays
topics.short: England's kings from Richard II to Richard III: crowns lost and won, and Falstaff in the tavern.

topics.title: Shakespeare: Julius Caesar and the Roman Plays
topics.short: Brutus and the conspirators kill Caesar for the Republic's sake, and the speeches after decide what follows.

topics.title: Shakespeare: Hamlet
topics.short: A prince told by his father's ghost to take revenge, and all the thinking that delays him.

topics.title: Shakespeare: Othello
topics.short: A trusted officer poisons a general's mind with lies, and jealousy does the rest.

topics.title: Shakespeare: King Lear
topics.short: An old king divides his kingdom by who flatters him best, and learns too late which daughter loves him.

topics.title: Shakespeare: Macbeth
topics.short: A brave soldier hears a prophecy, murders his king, and is undone by ambition and guilt.

topics.title: Shakespeare: The Tempest and the Late Plays
topics.short: Lost children found and old wrongs forgiven, ending with a magician who sets his magic aside.

topics.title: Shakespeare: The Sonnets
topics.short: 154 fourteen-line poems about love, friendship, time and whether verse can outlast it.

topics.title: Cervantes: Don Quixote, Part One
topics.short: A country gentleman reads so many romances that he rides out as a knight, with Sancho Panza beside him.

topics.title: Cervantes: Don Quixote, Part Two
topics.short: Now famous from Part One, the knight meets readers of his own story, and Sancho governs an island.
